ai.title: git metrics handle empty repos
ai.summary: getRepoMetrics in npm-app/src/utils/git.ts catches isomorphic-git log() rejections on empty repos. Returns empty ReadCommitResult[] array, logs 'Error fetching git log. Is this an empty git repo?'. Prevents unhandled promise rejection during metrics collection.

eli5.text: If you open a project that has no commits yet (an empty git repo), the system now stops crashing and instead quietly notes that there's nothing to measure, returning an empty list. This means internal tooling that collects git statistics no longer fails on brand-new repositories, and you won't see error messages or sudden stops when running those tools against a fresh project.

ai.title: Reorder git add in nested repo checkpoints
ai.summary: Moved `gitAddAll` invocation before nested repo detection loop in `npm-app/src/checkpoints/file-manager.ts`. Simplified `hasUnsavedChanges` to check raw output presence. Ensures staged files are added before checking for nested repos to prevent race conditions or missed changes.

eli5.text: When you save a checkpoint of your work, the system now stages your changes first and then checks for any nested sub-projects, instead of doing it in the reverse order. This prevents a situation where some of your edits might be missed because they were checked before being properly staged. You wouldn't notice a visible difference, but your saved checkpoints are now more reliable about capturing all your changes correctly.

ai.title: Support file:// prefix in ensureUrlProtocol
ai.summary: Updated `ensureUrlProtocol` in `common/src/util/string.ts` to preserve existing `file://` prefixes and automatically prepend `file://` to absolute paths starting with `/`. This prevents absolute file paths from being incorrectly treated as domains and prefixed with `https://` or `http://`. Affects shared core utility functions.

eli5.text: When you give the assistant a file path that starts with a slash, like /Users/name/notes.txt, it now opens the file directly instead of trying to load it as a web address. The assistant also stops adding http:// to paths that already use the file:// format, so those links keep working as intended. This applies to anyone using file paths with the assistant today. If you handed it an absolute path before, it would have guessed you meant a website; now it treats it like the local file it is.

ai.title: Fix login URL opening on Windows
ai.summary: The CLI login flow now correctly opens the browser on Windows by detecting the platform and using `start` instead of `open`. Previously, the hardcoded `open` command failed on non-Unix systems. This change is isolated to `npm-app/src/client.ts`.

eli5.text: When you try to log in, your computer was supposed to open your web browser automatically so you could sign in, but on Windows PCs it wasn't working at all. Now it does: the program checks what kind of computer you're using and opens the browser the right way for Windows, so you won't have to click a link manually anymore. This only affects people using the command-line tool to log in, and it's already live.

ai.title: Relax knowledge file update guidance in main-prompt
ai.summary: Removed the 'high bar' qualifier from the instruction prompting the agent to update knowledge files in backend/src/main-prompt.ts. This change aims to encourage more frequent knowledge base updates by lowering the perceived threshold for what constitutes 'useful' information. The modification affects the system prompt sent to the model during non-first user messages.

eli5.text: Starting today, the assistant will update its notes more often during conversations. There is no longer a strict requirement to only save information that is exceptionally important or hard to figure out from the code; instead, the assistant simply needs to decide whether saving a piece of information would help in the future. This means you should notice the assistant keeping better track of helpful details it learns while working with you.

ai.title: Prevent git root detection in home directory
ai.summary: New `isValidProjectRoot` helper in `npm-app/src/project-files.ts` checks if a directory is a subdirectory of the home dir using `isSubdir`. `findGitRoot` in `npm-app/src/utils/git.ts` now rejects roots that fail this check, preventing accidental project initialization in `$HOME`. The greeting logic in `npm-app/src/menu.ts` was updated to use this new helper instead of direct `isSubdir` calls.

eli5.text: If you start the assistant from inside your home folder, it will no longer treat that folder as a project to work on and will skip the normal welcome message it tries to show in that spot. Behind the scenes, the tool now double-checks that the folder it’s about to use as your project isn’t actually the same as (or inside) your home directory, and if it is, it ignores it instead of trying to set up a project there. This only affects people who happen to launch the assistant from within their home directory; everyone else sees no difference.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.318
ai.summary: Package version in npm-app/package.json incremented from 1.0.317 to 1.0.318. Internal release management.

eli5.text: You didn't get any new features today. This was just a behind-the-scenes update that increments the software's version number, which is a routine step that keeps your installed version current and ready for future feature releases. The actual new functionality for organizations and developers arrived in recent days, but this version bump simply packages those earlier changes together so they install cleanly.

ai.title: Add duration to main prompt logging
ai.summary: Added duration calculation to main prompt logging in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. Captures start time and logs elapsed milliseconds for prompt and response iterations. Internal observability change.

eli5.text: When the system runs your request through its internal process, it now quietly records how long each step takes in the background, so technical teams can spot slowdowns later. Nothing changes for you as you chat; this is purely behind-the-scenes logging for the team that maintains the system. If you were looking at internal logs, youd see timing information next to each processing step that was not there before.

ai.title: Remove env ENV from default ignored paths
ai.summary: Renamed DEFAULT_IGNORED_FILES to DEFAULT_IGNORED_PATHS and removed bare 'env' and 'ENV' entries from common/src/constants.ts. Eliminates over-broad matching that could ignore legitimate directories named env. Updates references in common/src/project-file-tree.ts for getProjectFileTree and isFileIgnored. Scoped to Shared/Core constants and file tree logic.

eli5.text: If you have a project folder that contains a directory literally named "env" or "ENV", the system used to automatically skip over it without looking inside, as if it were a secret configuration folder. This could cause you to miss real files you expected to see, simply because of the folder's name. The system now only skips folders with the standard hidden names like ".env", so ordinary directories called "env" get the attention they deserve. This change is live today and affects anything that builds a list of your project's files.

ai.title: Switch git-evals to experimental cost mode
ai.summary: Daily git-evals now use 'experimental' cost mode instead of 'normal'. This enables testing of Gemini models within the evaluation harness. Change applies to evals/git-evals/run-git-evals.ts via new COST_MODE constant.

eli5.text: The internal evaluation system that automatically checks the assistant daily has switched to a new testing mode. Instead of using the standard setup, it now tries out experimental model options (specifically Gemini) during these daily checks. If you were watching one of these background tests run, you would see it taking a slightly different path to test out the new approach. This only affects the internal testing infrastructure, not anything regular users experience.

ai.title: Fix whitespace squashing logic in display.ts
ai.summary: Replaced naive regex newline collapsing with `squashNewlines` in `npm-app/src/display.ts`. New logic strips OSC/CSI sequences and zero-width chars via `string-width` to detect true whitespace-only lines. Prevents false positives where ANSI codes looked like empty lines. Updates `previous` state tracking to use `PREFIX` (`.\r\n`) for robust line boundary detection.

eli5.text: When you run programs in this tool, the assistant keeps track of where lines of text begin and end to avoid printing too many blank lines. The old method guessed using a simple count of recent characters, which mistook colored text codes (invisible instructions that change colors or move the cursor) for actual blank lines, causing it to wrongly merge or split your output. The new method carefully reads each line, strips out all invisible formatting codes and zero-width characters, and only then decides whether a line is truly empty, using a more reliable marker to know when one line ends and the next begins. This is a behind-the-scenes housekeeping fix that makes the text output you see cleaner and less jumpy, especially when programs print styled text.
